solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Born just as clever

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for born, as in genealogies
just means fair or right

explanation.surface: A child described as clever from birth.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright pupil is an intelligent one, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Help with strike causing strong negative reaction

parts.note: to back someone is to help or support them
to lash is to strike

explanation.surface: Supporting a strike provokes hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlash is a hostile counter-reaction, especially of the public to a change.

clue.text: Hard-working Dutch American involved in our sit-in surprisingly

indicators.note: the abbreviations go inside the jumbled letters
surprisingly signals the letters land in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A diligent Dutch-American joins a sit-in protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges OUR SIT-IN; 'involved in' puts DUS inside, after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrious means diligent, always busy with work.

clue.text: Address husband trouble

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Speaking to a spouse about marital difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail someone is to call out to them, to address them.

clue.text: Degrades revolutionary when in prison? Just the opposite

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary

indicators.note: in would put the revolutionary inside the prison word
this reverses the previous instruction, so the prison word goes inside the revolutionary and when words instead

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a pen is an enclosure, slang for a prison

explanation.surface: A jailed revolutionary loses dignity, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites putting Che in jail; 'Just the opposite' cancels that order, so the jail goes inside the revolutionary instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheapen something is to lower its worth or dignity, which is to degrade it.

clue.text: Devout around place of retreat in truth

indicators.note: the devout word goes round the retreat word

parts.note: holy means pious, devout
a nest is a snug refuge

explanation.surface: A pious person in a retreat house, genuinely.
explanation.definitionFit: Honestly is used to mean truly, really, as in 'honestly, I did'.

clue.text: A pair point out a ghost

indicators.note: out here means the letters are out of place, in disorder

explanation.surface: Two people spot a spook.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparition is a ghostly figure that appears, a spectre.

clue.text: Fast mover running through desolate mudflats

indicators.note: the answer runs through the clue words, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Something quick dashing across bleak tidal flats.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird that runs at speed.

clue.text: Covering last of speeches by former PM

indicators.note: the final letter of speeches

parts.note: Edward Heath was British Prime Minister 1970-74

explanation.surface: Reporting on the final speech of an ex-premier.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting cover, as for a blade.

clue.text: Record breaking rave needing Tottenham's foremost warehouse

indicators.note: the record breaks into the party word

parts.note: a do is a party, like a rave
an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: foremost picks the first letter of Tottenham's

explanation.surface: A record-setting party needing a football club's lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a storehouse, a place where goods are kept.

clue.text: Fish oil's essence obtained by Gene not originally as an analgesic

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish

indicators.note: the oil's centre is taken in by the name, sitting inside its letters
the name loses its first letter, its original one
the essence of a word is its central letter, here the middle of oil

explanation.surface: Someone called Gene gets fish-oil extract and uses it as a painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not originally' removes G from GENE to leave ENE; 'obtained by' puts I, the middle of 'oil's', inside it to give EINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Codeine is an opiate drug widely used to relieve pain, so it is an example of an analgesic.

clue.text: Roman god's sister admitting weird pet hate finally

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the shuffled letters go inside the sister word

parts.note: a sister in a religious order is a nun

indicators.note: weird signals the letters of pet are rearranged
finally picks the last letter of hate

explanation.surface: A deity's sister takes in a strange pet that hates.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune was the Roman deity of the sea, the counterpart of Greek Poseidon.

clue.text: What Dr Manette needed to survive

definitions.meaning: Dr Manette in Dickens's A Tale of Two Cities made shoes in prison, so needed a shoemaker's foot-shaped mould

explanation.surface: The prisoner in A Tale of Two Cities and what kept him going.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Manette, imprisoned in the Bastille, kept his sanity by shoemaking, which needs a last.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler's last is the form a shoe is shaped on; as a verb last means endure.

clue.text: Against aim to block street by force

parts.note: con is against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: the aim word blocks the street by sitting in the middle of its letters

parts.note: to train a gun is to aim it

explanation.surface: A protest against plans to block a street using force.
explanation.definitionFit: Constraint is compulsion or restriction, the force that limits what one may do.

clue.text: Realist and old society tease become incompatible

indicators.note: to tease wool or hair is to pull it apart, so these letters are disentangled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A realist and an old club rib each other until they fall out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-assorted means badly matched, its members not suited to each other.

clue.text: Stop opening of trail after bears get sick

indicators.note: after says the trail letter is placed behind the bears word, not before it

parts.note: stands means bears, tolerates

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: Hikers halt at a trailhead after bears fall ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the trail letter after STANDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A standstill is a halt, a complete stop.

clue.text: Fairy prince putting on a spectacle for the audience

indicators.note: the prince is put on, worn, by the spectacle word, so it sits inside it
says the word for spectacle is what listeners hear, spelt another way

parts.note: a sight is a spectacle, something worth seeing

explanation.surface: A royal staging a show for an audience, though here it is a fairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the audience' means the spelling follows the sound of the word for a spectacle, not its usual spelling; 'putting on' means the prince is worn inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is a small elf or supernatural spirit of folklore, a kind of fairy.

clue.text: Gore counted around fifty in total

indicators.note: the first name and counted words go round the numeral

parts.note: Al Gore, the former US vice-president
told is an old sense of counted, as in telling beads or votes
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Al Gore tallying about fifty votes in total.
explanation.definitionFit: All told is an idiom meaning when everything is counted, altogether.

clue.text: Unrivalled nobles overwhelming the French

indicators.note: overwhelming means engulfing, so the nobles surround the article

parts.note: peers are nobles
les is French for the, with a plural noun

explanation.surface: Unmatched aristocrats crushing the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Peerless means without equal, which is unrivalled.

clue.text: Cool object placed by crew say on bow of Iranian launch

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool
it is an object, as a pronoun

indicators.note: the bow is the front of a boat, so the first letter of Iranian
say tells you the crew word is to be taken as heard

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew

explanation.surface: A cool item placed by a rowing crew on the bow of an Iranian vessel at launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns EIGHT, a rowing crew, into its sound-alike ATE; 'on' puts it after I.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate something is to start it off, to launch it.

clue.text: Advice from uncle so ridiculous

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests the letters are made absurd, jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: An uncle's guidance that is ludicrous.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel is guidance given to someone, a synonym of advice.

clue.text: Tax return at home may be alarming

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, an alarm, which is alarming by nature

indicators.note: return here means the tax word goes back the other way

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free
in means at home

explanation.surface: Filing a tax return from home can be scary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax return' reads like a form; scot is an old tax, kept in 'scot-free'. 'return' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is an alarm bell or warning signal, something whose job is to alarm.

clue.text: Clergyman's answer? Finding company in haunt of vice

indicators.note: the answer and company go inside the haunt word

parts.note: a den is a disreputable haunt, as in a den of iniquity

explanation.surface: A cleric's reply on being found with friends in a den of iniquity.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is a church minister ranking below a priest, a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Contributing to obscure beliefs of Jack Cade perhaps

indicators.note: Contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something feeding into the murky ideas of a historical figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led the 1450 Kent uprising against Henry VI. 'of' with 'perhaps' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Cade led a revolt against the crown, so he is an example of a rebel.

clue.text: Emended part of the essay on Republican support returning in an affluent state

indicators.note: emended means corrected, so these letters are reworked
part of picks just the opening letter of the
returning says the support word is written backwards

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: Revising an essay that supports Republicans, written by someone well off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emended' is the anagram signal; 'part of the' is just its first letter; 'returning' reverses the golf support; 'on' puts the later pieces after the essay.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on easy street is an idiom for living in comfort and wealth.

clue.text: Left with soldiers in the middle of exercises

indicators.note: the soldiers sit inside the exercises abbreviation

parts.note: PT is physical training, exercises
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Abandoned with troops mid-drill.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, port is the left-hand side when facing forward.

clue.text: Give up for a month around the start of Easter

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the month is written backwards

parts.note: DEC is the abbreviation for December

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Abstaining for a month either side of Easter, as in Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to surrender or yield something, to give it up.

clue.text: Cup of tea left to cool

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
to ice something is to cool it

explanation.surface: A cup of tea set aside to go cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalice is a goblet, especially a ceremonial drinking cup used at communion.

clue.text: Wise son leaving for a long time

indicators.note: the son leaves, so his letter is removed

parts.note: sage means wise

explanation.surface: A wise son departing for a long spell.
explanation.definitionFit: An age, or ages, is colloquially a very long period.

clue.text: Choice by Priam oddly ignored in play

parts.note: elect as an adjective means chosen, choice

indicators.note: the odd letters are dropped, leaving the even letters of the name

explanation.surface: King Priam's selection passed over in a stage drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is a Greek tragedy by Sophocles, and also by Euripides, so it is a play.

clue.text: Small tip of steel on goad is not necessary

parts.note: to needle someone is to goad them

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tiny steel point on a cattle prod is superfluous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the small pieces after the goad word.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means unnecessary, not needed.

clue.text: Unfortunate debacle not initially caused by university official

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests the letters have gone wrong and are reordered
the first letter of caused is to be left out of the anagram

explanation.surface: A sorry fiasco blamed on a college functionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' takes C (the start of 'caused') out of DEBACLE, and 'Unfortunate' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A beadle is a ceremonial officer at some universities, who leads processions.
